Turns off the experimental welcome page. Its sign-in button label is a literal "Continue with GitHub" and the provider it signs into is a hardcoded 'github' (onboardingVariationA.ts:707), while the surrounding terms text correctly reads Novel Builder because that part comes from product.json. On this product it therefore signs into a provider that does not exist, which is what produced two disagreeing states: an account menu showing a valid Novel Builder session and a chat surface insisting the user is signed out. Upstream holds nothing at this key.

upstream ships no default here, so the agent host refuses to run while the chat session is signed out. Our auth is a different provider and the host's signed-in probe does not see it; without this default the agent silently declines to start for an author who is in fact signed in. If upstream ever ships its own default, re-derive rather than keep ours.

upstream ships 1.0.11. We build against open-vsx, not Microsoft's marketplace, and open-vsx does not mirror Microsoft's 1.0.11 .vsix — it serves its own rebuild (604KB unpacked against 2.4MB, no ThirdPartyNotices), so the sha256 upstream records can never match and the build dies on a checksum mismatch. 1.0.10 on open-vsx IS byte-identical to Microsoft's, so pinning there keeps a checksum we can actually verify against an independent record rather than blessing bytes nobody else vouches for. Re-derive when open-vsx mirrors a later version, or when we decide a novel editor should not be shipping a JavaScript CPU-profile viewer at all.
